topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, target audience, and key learning outcomes regarding cancer biology.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Cellular Differentiation and Tissue Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe cancer as a disruption of normal differentiation programs and three-dimensional tissue organization driven by progressive genetic alterations.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Stepwise Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how local tissue invasion, metastatic spread, and stepwise histological changes distinguish benign tumors from malignant cancers.

topics.label: Principles of Tumor Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and exceptions used to name benign and malignant tumors according to their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the anatomical and physiological mechanisms through which primary and secondary tumors cause systemic illness and death.

topics.label: Comparative Cancer Incidence Across Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of tumor incidence and mortality in human populations and across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Cancer Detection and Screening Modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the clinical rationale, histological basis, and relative effectiveness of population screening methods across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the session with a recap of learning outcomes and logistical notes for upcoming practicals.
